### Additional Information (optional)

The original public source for the application is `curatedMetagenomicData` (Pasolli et al., *Nature Methods* 14, 1023–1024, 2017; doi:10.1038/nmeth.4468). The supplied processed CSV files document the starting point of the prior submitted application workflow. Full upstream acquisition and preprocessing, the final Round 2 application figure lineage, and permission to redistribute each processed or generated file remain subject to Section 5 coauthor confirmation. The technical 50-repeat studies are represented by saved seed-level results, selected detailed RDS files, source code, and provenance records. The complete transformed 20D BART RDS set is approximately 14 GB and is not included; its seed-level summaries and recomputation code are included.

# Part 2: Code

## Abstract

The archive contains an anonymized local source package, `ReviewPkg` 0.0.0.9001, corresponding to the implementation used by the Round 2 simulations, the prior submitted method and comparator source, scripts for simulation, summarization, and figure rendering, and release-specific commands for drawing and light runs. Saved seed-level results permit regeneration of the technical tables and most figures without rerunning all 50 seeds. The Section 5 code and inputs are included as prior-submission reference material pending final coauthor confirmation.

### Supporting software requirements

#### Version of primary software used

The original and local Round 2 checks used R 4.5.2. The portable table command was checked with Python 3.14.4 and uses only the Python standard library. A compatible C++ compiler toolchain is needed to install the bundled R source packages. The Section 5 Python environment and its final code path require coauthor confirmation.

#### Libraries and dependencies used by the code

`code/methods/ReviewPkg/` contains the anonymized Round 2 method source, version 0.0.0.9001. It preserves the numerical implementation, defaults, and compiler options of the Round 2 source while using the anonymous package and function names established in Round 1. The unchanged Round 1 `ReviewPkg` 0.0.0.9000 and corrected `densratio` 0.2.1 are under `reference/r1/code/methods/`. The two method versions must be installed in separate local libraries and run in separate R processes.

Use `Rscript code/setup_review.R --variant=r2 --lib-dir=<new-r2-library>` to compile the supplied Round 2 source. For historical Round 1 execution, select `--variant=r1` and a different library. No public method repository is required. Anonymous source identifiers and release-file SHA-256 values provide the submitted provenance record; the mapping to original source identities is retained privately.

Current local checks used `Rcpp` 1.1.1-1, `RcppArmadillo` 14.4.1-1, `ggplot2` 4.0.3, `patchwork` 1.3.2, `scales` 1.4.0, `mvtnorm` 1.3-3, `pracma` 2.4.6, and `ada` 2.0-5, together with the supplied corrected `densratio`. Full Round 2 workflows additionally use `digest`, `matrixStats`, and `rpart`. See `ENVIRONMENT.md` and the verification records for the tested environment. **[AUTHOR TO COMPLETE a fully isolated dependency installation check and final dependency lock or equivalent version record.]**

#### Supporting system/hardware requirements (optional)

The anonymized and original Round 2 method sources were compiled with R 4.5.2 on Windows 11 x64 using Rtools45 / GCC 14.3.0. Twelve reduced test cases gave exactly identical fitted objects, predictions, posterior draws, and post-fit/post-prediction RNG states. The anonymous R2 light run for the displayed 2D local-shift seed took 355.9 seconds; its checks and limits are recorded in `VALIDATION_STATUS.md`. **[AUTHOR TO ADD complete peak-resource measurements and a fully isolated dependency test result.]** Full 50-seed recomputation is substantially more expensive; the supplied saved results support inspection without that rerun.

# Part 3: Reproducibility workflow

## Scope

The provided workflow reproduces:

- [ ] Any numbers provided in text in the paper
- [x] The computational method(s) presented in the paper (i.e., code is provided that implements the method(s))
- [ ] All tables and figures in the paper
- [x] Selected tables and figures in the paper, as explained and justified below:

The supplied saved inputs and commands regenerate Main Tables 1–2, the transformed 20D and CDC supplementary tables, and the technical main and supplementary figures described in `FIGURE_TABLE_MAP.md`. All 264 displayed numerical table entries were checked against the final local TeX after rounding to three decimals. All fifteen technical PDFs were regenerated from the anonymous candidate; fourteen match the corresponding manuscript assets pixel for pixel at 110 dpi. Current comparison records are in `verification/anonymous_20260928/`. Main Figure 2 can be regenerated at its fixed seed, although its current panel geometry differs from the manuscript PDF. Section 5 final figures remain pending coauthor confirmation of their Round 2 data and code lineage. The archive includes source scripts for full 50-seed recomputation; their full execution has not been repeated as part of anonymization, while the archive retains seed-level summaries and selected detailed RDS files for practical review. The light run uses the displayed data seed with reduced computational settings; its estimates can differ from the paper and are labeled `SMOKE_NOT_FOR_PAPER`.

### Instructions

Unzip the archive and work from `reproducibility_materials_anonymous/`. Read `README.md` for the directory layout, exact commands, and the requirement to write into a new output directory outside the supplied `reference/` and `results/` trees. `FIGURE_TABLE_MAP.md` identifies each technical table and figure, its saved inputs, code, and verification status. `ENVIRONMENT.md` documents anonymous source identifiers and locally tested dependencies; `VALIDATION_STATUS.md` records completed checks and unresolved items. Verify the package inventory with `python code/verify_bundle.py`.

Install the anonymous method source using `code/setup_review.R` as described in Part 2. The default light runner requires the R2 method version; use `--source-variant=r1` with the separate R1 library only for historical checks. R2 coverage and boosting commands verify the release source manifest; the global/null runners use `--release-id` with the value in `RELEASE_ID.txt`, so the review workflow does not require an identifying Git checkout.

For the four technical tables, run `python code/portable/reproduce_tables.py <new-output-dir>`. The README gives individual drawing commands for the main and supplementary figures; each command takes saved results and writes to a separate new output directory. To exercise a simulation computation at the displayed 2D Figure 3 seed, use `Rscript code/light/run_light.R --family=2d --scenario=local_shift --n0=5000 --n1=5000 --seed=1 --lib-dir=<installed-R-library> --output-dir=<new-output-dir>`. For the 20D supplementary location surface, use the same entry point with `--family=20d --scenario=latent_location_shift --n0=5000 --n1=5000 --seed=21`. The 2D supplementary surface settings and data seeds are listed in `FIGURE_TABLE_MAP.md`. These reduced runs use the selected method source with archived light hyperparameters. They are workflow checks; the archived seed-level results are used for the reported 50-repeat summaries.
